Land Forces 2026 puts manufacturers at the centre of Defence opportunity

by Jack Lloyd
September 9, 2026
in Defence, Features
Reading Time: 4 mins read
A A

Land Forces 2026 will unite Defence personnel, government representatives, prime contractors, SMEs, technology developers, researchers and manufacturers. Image: AMDA

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:02
Instaread

From supply chain engagement to innovation and thought leadership, Land Forces 2026 is set to connect Australian manufacturers with the people shaping the future of Defence.

Returning as one of Australia’s largest international land defence expositions and forums, Land Forces 2026 will once again unite Defence personnel, government representatives, prime contractors, SMEs, technology developers, researchers and manufacturers from Australia and overseas. Land Forces has also evolved into a broader industry engagement platform, combining networking, policy discussions, technical presentations and innovation showcases designed to help businesses better understand where they fit within Australia’s defence ecosystem.

Connecting industry with Defence priorities

According to AMDA Foundation, the event organiser, one of Land Forces’ greatest strengths is the accessibility of its conference and presentation program. Visitor registration provides complimentary access across all three days of the exhibition, including entry to the exhibition floor and most conference sessions running throughout the event.

Trade Visitor registration is available to individuals working in, or affiliated with, defence and related industries, while Defence Visitor registration is open to personnel holding valid Australian or international defence identification credentials.

Throughout the event, attendees will hear from organisations like the Australian Army, Department of Defence, Defence Delivery Group, Guided Weapons Explosive Ordnance Enterprise (GWEO), Austrade, the US Commercial Service and the Advanced Strategic Capabilities Accelerator (ASCA) will provide updates on procurement priorities, capability development, export opportunities and industry participation.

The Australian Army will also play a central role throughout Land Forces 2026, with a program designed to strengthen dialogue between Defence and industry.

Among the headline sessions will be the Chief of Army Symposium, Army Innovation Day and the Junior Leader Forum. These sessions are designed to provide industry with a deeper understanding of Army’s future requirements, operational priorities and innovation challenges.

The Hub brings industry conversations together

The Hub adds another dimension to the Land Forces experience by creating a dedicated platform for thought leadership and practical industry discussion. Open to all trade badge holders and fully integrated into the broader conference program, The Hub will host experts from across government, Defence, industry and academia, exploring the strategic, technological and industrial issues shaping Australia’s defence future.

Running across all three days of the event in the BelleVue Ballroom at the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre, the program will focus on practical conversations that matter to manufacturers.

Topics include government funding opportunities for defence businesses, resilience across Australia’s industrial base, optimised supply chains, workforce and salary trends, industrialising munitions manufacturing, artificial intelligence, defence manufacturing resilience through additive manufacturing, contested logistics and intellectual property protection.

Other sessions examine Australia’s future defence posture, Army’s enhanced littoral manoeuvre capability, large-scale solid rocket motor manufacturing and the growing role of quantum computing and high-performance computing within Defence.

For manufacturers, The Hub offers an opportunity to move beyond product demonstrations and engage with broader strategic questions surrounding workforce capability, sovereign manufacturing and emerging technologies. Also, it provides an environment where industry peers, government representatives and Defence stakeholders can exchange ideas and build new partnerships.

Showcasing Australia’s innovators

Innovation has long been a defining feature of Australia’s defence industry, and Land Forces 2026 is placing even greater emphasis on recognising and accelerating new ideas through the return of the Innovation Pitchfest and Awards.

Designed as a national showcase for Australian innovation, the program provides organisations, researchers, SMEs and emerging innovators with an opportunity to present breakthrough technologies to an international audience of Defence representatives, investors, industry partners and potential customers.

Innovations are recognised across four categories: the Innovation Award, Emerging Technology Award, Young Innovator Award and Blue-Sky Thinking Innovation Award, reflecting the breadth of Australia’s innovation ecosystem from early-stage concepts through to commercially mature technologies.

Following a competitive judging process, finalists will deliver live presentations during Land Forces, with category winners to be announced onsite. Winners of the Innovation Award, Emerging Technology Award and Young Innovator Award will each receive a $30,000 cash prize, while the Blue-Sky Thinking Innovation Award winner will receive $10,000 to further support personal and innovation development. A Best Presenter Award will also recognise excellence in communicating new ideas to industry audiences.

This year’s projects as a part of the pitchfest range from sovereign intelligence systems developed by BlakBox, advanced electronic warfare concepts from the Australian Army, AI-driven capability forecasting by Cyndr and UNSW, new body armour technology from Chiron Global Tech, augmented reality display systems developed by the University of Melbourne, innovative deployable infrastructure from Varley and medical technologies designed to address defence-specific injuries.

Introducing the Innovation Base: 

For the very first time at Land Forces, Innovation Pitchfest and Awards finalists will present their ideas and technologies in a dedicated precinct. The finalists will showcase their concepts in a purpose-built exhibit featuring a dedicated pod. Visitors will have the opportunity to explore new ideas, meet the innovators behind them, and learn more about the technologies shaping the future of defence capability.

Register now

Visitor registration for Land Forces 2026 is now open and free for eligible trade and Defence attendees at https://landforces.com.au/registration/.
